title: Targeting the Essential Transcription Factor HP1043 of Helicobacter pylori: A Drug Repositioning Study.
authors: Antoniciello, Federico; Roncarati, Davide; Zannoni, Annamaria; Chiti, Elena; Scarlato, Vincenzo; Chiappori, Federica
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子对接和MMGBSA分子动力学模拟筛选已知药物靶向幽门螺杆菌必需转录因子HP1043，抑制其与DNA启动子结合，属于TF-DNA互作体系且采用物理模拟方法，但聚焦药物重定位而非结合机制建模，故评7分。
abstract: Antibiotic-resistant bacterial pathogens are a very challenging problem nowadays. Helicobacter pylori is one of the most widespread and successful human pathogens since it colonizes half of the world population causing chronic and atrophic gastritis, peptic ulcer, mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue-lymphoma, and even gastric adenocarcinoma. Moreover, it displays resistance to numerous antibiotics. One of the H. pylori pivotal transcription factors, HP1043, plays a fundamental role in regulating essential cellular processes. Like other bacterial transcription factors, HP1043 does not display a eukaryote homolog. These characteristics make HP1043 a promising candidate to develop novel antibacterial strategies. Drug repositioning is a relatively recent strategy employed in drug development; testing approved drugs on new targets considerably reduces the time and cost of this process. The combined computational and in vitro approach further reduces the number of compounds to be tested in vivo. Our aim was to identify a subset of known drugs able to prevent HP1043 binding to DNA promoters. This result was reached through evaluation by molecular docking the binding capacity of about 14,350 molecules on the HP1043 dimer in both conformations, bound and unbound to the DNA. Employing an ad hoc pipeline including MMGBSA molecular dynamics, a selection of seven drugs was obtained. These were tested in vitro by electrophoretic mobility shift assay to evaluate the HP1043-DNA interaction. Among these, three returned promising results showing an appreciable reduction of the DNA-binding activity of HP1043. Overall, we applied a computational methodology coupled with experimental validation of the results to screen a large number of known drugs on one of the H. pylori essential transcription factors. This methodology allowed a rapid reduction of the number of drugs to be tested, and the drug repositioning approach considerably reduced the drug design costs. Identified drugs do not belong to the same pharmaceutical category and, by computational analysis, bound different cavities, but all display a reduction of HP1043 binding activity on the DNA.
abstract_zh: 抗生素耐药性细菌病原体是当今一个极具挑战性的问题。幽门螺杆菌（Helicobacter pylori）是最广泛且最成功的人类病原体之一，因为它定植于全球一半人口，导致慢性及萎缩性胃炎、消化性溃疡、黏膜相关淋巴组织淋巴瘤，甚至胃腺癌。此外，它对多种抗生素表现出耐药性。HP1043是幽门螺杆菌的关键转录因子之一，在调控必需细胞过程中发挥基础性作用。与其他细菌转录因子一样，HP1043没有真核生物同源物。这些特性使HP1043成为开发新型抗菌策略的有前景的候选靶点。药物重定位（drug repositioning）是药物开发中相对较新的策略；在新型靶点上测试已批准药物可显著减少该过程的时间和成本。计算与体外方法相结合进一步减少了需在体内测试的化合物数量。我们的目标是识别一组已知药物，能够阻止HP1043与DNA启动子结合。这一结果通过分子对接（molecular docking）评估约14,350个分子在HP1043二聚体两种构象（与DNA结合和未结合状态）上的结合能力而实现。采用包括MMGBSA分子动力学（molecular dynamics）在内的定制流程，筛选出七种药物。这些药物通过电泳迁移率变动分析（electrophoretic mobility shift assay）在体外测试，以评估HP1043-DNA相互作用。其中三种显示出有希望的结果，显著降低了HP1043的DNA结合活性。总体而言，我们应用了计算方法结合实验验证来筛选大量已知药物，针对幽门螺杆菌的一个必需转录因子。该方法允许快速减少待测试药物数量，且药物重定位方法显著降低了药物设计成本。识别出的药物不属于同一药物类别，并通过计算分析结合于不同空腔，但均显示出对HP1043在DNA上结合活性的降低作用。
